Ship agent-generated code with murmur-level confidence.

Murmur is the reliability harness that validates every coding-agent output against deterministic test suites, consensus models, and drift monitors — so your pipeline stays predictable even when the model isn't.

Get started on GitHub See how it works

Reliability metrics at a glance

pass@1
94.7%

First-pass accuracy across 12k HumanEval-style benchmarks

passk
98.3%

Consensus score with k‑3 majority-vote sampling

variance
±1.2%

Output drift measured across five consecutive runs

Why teams run Murmur in CI

Deterministic verification

Every agent output is run through a hermetic sandbox with reproducible test suites. Murmur catches regressions, hallucinations, and subtle logic errors before they reach a pull request. No more "looks good to me" on broken code.

Multi-pass consensus scoring

Murmur samples the same prompt k times and cross-validates results. When outputs diverge, the harness surfaces the discrepancy with a diff and a confidence score. You set the threshold; Murmur enforces it.

Drift monitoring over time

Model updates, prompt tweaks, and temperature shifts all introduce drift. Murmur snapshots benchmark baselines and alerts you when pass@1 or variance moves outside your tolerance band — so reliability is measurable, not anecdotal.

Every murmur in your agent pipeline, caught before it fails.

Murmur is the open-source reliability harness that stress-tests coding agents across thousands of discrete tasks — flagging regressions, hallucinations, and silent drift the moment they appear.

Continuous Monitoring

Murmur wraps your agent in a lightweight scaffold that logs every tool call, token emission, and file mutation. Regressions are flagged the instant a previously-solved task breaks.

Deterministic Verification

A pluggable verifier pipeline runs unit tests, diff checks, and behavioral assertions against every agent output. No more guessing whether a patch actually fixes the bug.

Consensus Sampling

By running multiple independent passes and comparing outputs, Murmur identifies high-variance prompts and brittle generations — giving you a statistical grip on reliability.

Your agents write code.
Murmur makes it reliable.

An open-source reliability harness that evaluates coding agents on every commit. Measure pass@1 accuracy, pass^k consistency, and run-to-run variance so your team ships with evidence — not wishful thinking.

Get Started Read the Docs →

What Murmur measures

Pass@1 Accuracy

Does your agent produce a correct solution on the first attempt? Murmur benchmarks pass@1 across hundreds of real-world coding tasks, giving you a single-number reliability score that tracks with production outcomes.

Pass^k Consistency

How often does at least one of k samples pass? Pass^k reveals whether your agent benefits from retries — critical for understanding reliability at scale when you can afford multiple generation attempts.

Variance Tracking

A single score is a snapshot. Murmur tracks pass-rate variance across multiple evaluation runs, surfacing flaky behaviors and regressions before they erode trust in your agent pipeline.

Live Reliability Metrics

Aggregated from the Murmur public benchmark suite — updated hourly.

pass^k (k=5) 96.1% At least one of five passes
variance ±2.8% Run-to-run deviation

Agent Reliability, Measured

Three signals that tell you whether your coding agents are ready for production.

01

Pass@1 Monitoring

Track first-attempt pass rates across every agent in your fleet. Murmur captures each evaluation run, surfaces regressions instantly, and lets you ship agent updates with data-driven confidence — no guesswork required.

02

Passk Consistency

A single pass can be luck. Murmur computes passk across multiple independent samples to reveal true consistency. Know whether your agent genuinely understands the task or just happened to get it right once.

03

Variance Tracking

Identical prompts should yield stable results. Murmur tracks output variance over time, alerting you the moment agent behavior drifts so you can investigate and remediate before your users notice a thing.
